# contextbill

> Local-first cost analysis for Claude Code. Reads the transcripts already on your
> disk and prices them at Anthropic API rates: which sessions ran expensive, which
> produced nothing, and how much of the total is fixed context loaded on every turn.

contextbill exists because per-seat billing reports one number a month, which is
enough to know you spent money and not enough to know where. It ships in two
forms that share one analysis engine, so both produce the same figures for the
same input.

## What it does

- Prices every turn against a dated rate table, split by model, and by whether
  tokens were input, output, a cache write or a cache read.
- Separates the startup prefix (system prompt, tool catalog, connector
  definitions, instruction files) from the work you actually asked for. That
  prefix is written to cache once and re-read on every subsequent turn, so a
  long session pays for it repeatedly. On the corpus it was built against it was
  18.2% of the bill.
- Attributes spend to categories such as browser automation, shell, file
  operations and connector catalogs, so the expensive habit is identifiable.
- Keeps saved reports so a number can be compared against itself over time.

## The two surfaces

- **Command line**: `npx contextbill`. Zero runtime dependencies, no network
  access of any kind, writes a self-contained HTML report. Nothing is uploaded.
- **Hosted web app**: https://contextbill.vercel.app. Transcripts are parsed in
  the browser tab. Only aggregates reach the server: totals, per-model spend,
  per-category spend and per-session counts. Message content is never
  transmitted, and the database has no column that could store it.

## Privacy

- https://contextbill.vercel.app/privacy. What is stored, what is not, and why
  there is no cookie consent banner (the only cookie is the auth session).
- Project folder names encode an operating system username, so they are redacted
  before any report is saved.
- Row-level security in Postgres restricts every row to the account that created
  it.

## Accuracy note

Every figure is an estimate, not an invoice. Three limits, largest first.

Figures are API-equivalent: every dollar is what that usage would cost metered
at Anthropic's published first-party API rates. Most Claude Code usage is on a
subscription, which bills a flat fee, so the totals value the usage rather than
restate what anyone was charged. Bedrock and Vertex are priced separately again
and are not modelled.

A transcript records how many tokens were written to cache but not which cache
lifetime was billed, so contextbill assumes the cheaper one and tends to
understate rather than overstate.

The startup-prefix figure is a model of how fixed overhead is apportioned, not a
line item any provider bills separately.
